title: Fallen Journalists Memorial Act
official_summary:
Fallen Journalists Memorial Act

This bill authorizes the Fallen Journalists Memorial Foundation to establish a commemorative work on federal land in commemoration of America's commitment to a free press as represented by journalists who sacrificed their lives in service to that cause.

Federal funds may not be used to pay any expense for the establishment of the commemorative work.

The bill makes the Fallen Journalists Memorial Foundation solely responsible for acceptance of contributions and payment of the expenses for the establishment of the commemorative work.

summary.headline: A 2020 law lets a private foundation build a memorial on federal land honoring journalists who died in service to a free press, at no cost to taxpayers.
summary.what_it_does: The law authorizes the Fallen Journalists Memorial Foundation to set up a commemorative work on federal land. The work honors journalists who gave their lives while serving a free press. Federal money cannot be used for any part of establishing the memorial. The foundation alone must collect donations and pay all costs.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate effective date, so the law took effect when it was enacted on December 23, 2020.
